answer: Random Beacon Slot Admission. Each identity commits a registration hash before round R; after the verifiable beacon pulse publishes, hash(commitment, beacon) must fall below a threshold to transact that epoch. The log records requests like stacked timber, but beacon output is unknown at commit. A sonnet-length commitment is unnecessary; one hash binds the request. Attacker pays a nonrefundable request fee per commitment and waits one round; with fee 5 and admission 1%, expected cost is 500 per active identity.
